Plot a random forest

Source: R/random_forest.r
plot.ecodive_random_forest.Rd

Five views of a random_forest() result, drawn from the result alone:

Usage

# S3 method for class 'ecodive_random_forest'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("importance", "roc", "confusion", "predictions", "tuning"),
  n_features = 20,
  importance = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A random_forest() result.

type

Which view: 'importance', 'roc', 'confusion', 'predictions' or 'tuning'. Default: 'importance'

n_features

For 'importance': how many features to show. Default: 20

importance

For 'importance': 'impurity' or 'permutation'; NULL for the one the result was sorted by. Default: NULL

...

Passed on to the base plotting function (e.g. main, xlab, col).

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

  • 'importance' (the default): horizontal bars of the n_features most important features, largest at the top. With impurity importance, the full-data forest's values, with whiskers of the cross-validation folds' standard deviation; with permutation importance, the mean over trees, with whiskers of its standard error (SD / sqrt(trees)).

  • 'roc' (classification): the ROC curve of each class against the rest (one curve for two classes), and for more classes the micro and macro averages, with AUCs in the legend, as q2-sample-classifier draws them. Cross-validated (out of bag without cross-validation).

  • 'confusion' (classification): a heatmap of the confusion matrix, each observed class's row as proportions (shading) and counts (written).

  • 'predictions' (regression): cross-validated (or out-of-bag) predictions against the observed values, with the 1:1 line.

  • 'tuning' (with a grid): each grid point's out-of-bag error, one line per training set.

See also

random_forest()

Examples

    counts <- ex_counts[rep(1:4, each = 5), ] + outer(1:20, 1:6) %% 7
    site   <- rep(rownames(ex_counts), each = 5)
    fit    <- random_forest(counts, site, n_trees = 50, cpus = 1)
    plot(fit)

    plot(fit, 'roc')

    plot(fit, 'confusion')
